name: Write contacts
plain: Lets the app add, edit or delete address book entries.
meaning: Lets apps modify who is in the phone's book, which can plant fake contacts or merge entries. Backup and sync apps need it.

android.store_policy: Play: same data-safety rules as read
android.note: Granting READ_CONTACTS or WRITE_CONTACTS grants the whole contacts group.

ios.prompt_ui: Same prompt as read; no write-only option
ios.api_surface: CNSaveRequest, CNContactViewController (new contact UI without permission)
ios.note: iOS has no write-only contacts mode; UI controllers add a contact without access.

limits.headline: Can add, edit and delete address book entries once you tap Allow
limits.user_action: You tap Allow when a backup, sync or contacts app asks
can: Change many entries in one batch (Android)
cannot: Change contacts before you tap Allow
Get add only access on iPhone; it uses the same prompt as seeing contacts
Change the contacts group one part at a time on Android; one grant covers all
limits.differs: iPhone has no add only mode but a system new contact screen needs no access; Android groups seeing and changing contacts together.

story.what_it_is: Lets the app add, edit or delete entries in your address book.
story.for_you: A prompt asks to change your contacts. If you agree, the app can add people, fix numbers or remove entries. You may not notice until your address book looks different.
story.for_makers: A caller ID or backup app has to write to restore your contacts. The same power could add fake contacts or merge the wrong people. Platforms want apps to use the system editor when they can.

use_cases.example: A backup app restores your address book on a new phone.
A caller ID app adds the names of known businesses.
A company directory app adds coworkers to the phone's address book.
A social app adds friends' photos to contacts.
A shop app saves a delivery driver as a contact.
A malicious app could plant a fake bank number to run scams.

story.android_note: Granting read or write contacts permission grants the whole contacts permission group.
story.ios_note: iOS has no write only contacts mode, but the system editor can add one contact without access.

technical_bounds: Android groups permissions so one grant covers the group
Users can pick or save via system UI without any grant
User can remove the account from Settings to drop synced rows

linkedin.how: Android build 4.1.995 lists WRITE_SYNC_SETTINGS, the permission used by sync adapters. LinkedIn help states contacts sync has been removed, so the adapter is probably legacy; unverified.

history.change: Limited access also limits the write scope
Write to contacts needs a runtime grant
